blindSummary: This is a self-governing overseas territory of a distant metropolitan power whose law formally applies, but customary authority — three traditional kingdoms and the dominant church — dominates daily life; no visible LGBT presence; thin data.
blindOutOfScope: Overseas territory of a distant metropolitan state; local deviations as noted.
blindSourceSummaries: News feature (Jan 2018): trans women incarcerated in the metropolitan state on the basis of their legal gender fall into a legal gray area - the metropolitan state's law applies in this territory, so the finding carries over.

The metropolitan state's detention watchdog opinion of 25 May 2021 on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty (binding here through the metropolitan state's law): serious violations persist across places of detention.

Encyclopedia page on transgender rights in this territory: the metropolitan state's law applies - judicial gender-marker change without surgery or diagnosis since 2016-17 reforms; gender-identity anti-discrimination protections since 2012; but isolation, a population of ~11,000 and dominant-church plus indigenous cultural norms create practical barriers; no local specialists (patients must travel to the metropolitan state or a larger nearby territory); an established indigenous third-gender concept coexists with stigma; no non-binary recognition.

Country-of-origin information (COI) page on an asylum-research network for this territory: no COI experts or resources yet identified - directory placeholder with links to legal-assistance and LGBTQI+ resource pages.
The same network's LGBTQI+ resources page for this territory: a placeholder inviting contributions; no documented LGBTQI+ resources for the territory.
An LGBTQ+ travel-guide site's country page for this territory - equality index, gender-identity recognition, same-sex unions and marriage data (page largely navigation content at fetch time).
